# Number of Senior Citizens.

@example The ages are 61, 60 and 73; 60 is not over sixty.
["5550001234M6107","5550001235F6008","5550001236O7311"]
=> 2

@example The age is 09; the 62 after it is the seat number.
["8123456789F0962"]
=> 0

@example The ages 88 and 66 are over sixty; 12 and 30 are not.
["4471209988M8801","4471209989O1202","4471209990F6603","4471209991M3004"]
=> 2

# One record aged 61, the youngest age that counts.
["0000000000M6100"]
=> 1

# One record aged exactly 60.
["0000000001F6000"]
=> 0

# Ages 59, 60 and 61.
["1000000059M5901","1000000060F6002","1000000061O6103"]
=> 1

# The extreme ages 00 and 99.
["2000000000F0010","2000000099M9911"]
=> 1

# Every age from 60 to 69: the tens digit alone can't tell 60 from 61.
["3000000060M6020","3000000061F6121","3000000062O6222","3000000063M6323","3000000064F6424","3000000065O6525","3000000066M6626","3000000067F6727","3000000068O6828","3000000069M6929"]
=> 9

# Round ages 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90: a units digit of 0 doesn't rule out an
# age over sixty.
["4000000050M5031","4000000060F6032","4000000070O7033","4000000080M8034","4000000090F9035"]
=> 3

# Young riders (07, 16, 09) whose neighbouring digits look old: characters
# 12 and 13 read 79, 68 and 97, and the age with the seat after it reads
# 799, 1688 and 977.
["9876543299M0799","8888888877F1688","7777777766O0977"]
=> 0

# Old riders (71, 82, 64) whose neighbouring digits look young: characters
# 12 and 13 read 10, 20 and 40. Everyone counts.
["0000000101M7100","0000000102F8201","0000000103O6402"]
=> 3

# The same age several times: each record counts.
["5000000001F7710","5000000002F7711","5000000003M7712","5000000004O7713"]
=> 4

# Nobody over sixty, with 60 twice and a leading-zero age.
["6000000001M6040","6000000002F6041","6000000003O0042"]
=> 0
